patch_description: This approach replaces the laggy sliding-window average with a fundamentally different pipeline: (1) a robust noise estimate from first differences (MAD-based, insensitive to outliers), (2) a forward–backward (two-pass) constant-velocity Kalman smoother — running the filter forward then backward and optimally blending the two runs gives near-RTS-smoother quality with zero phase distortion, dramatically improving noise reduction and lag, and (3) a zero-phase Savitzky-Golay (local quadratic fit) smoothing pass with reflected-boundary padding to eliminate spurious slope reversals without adding delay. This combination directly targets the four objectives: slope-change/false-reversal counts collapse due to the polynomial smoothing stage, lag error is minimized by the zero-phase design and the trend (velocity) state, tracking accuracy is maintained by adaptive process noise that boosts gain when innovations grow, and computational cost remains O(n).
